tasks.query: parse an HTML string together with a base URI and a chosen parser instance into a document tree
tasks.note: Jsoup.parse(String html, String baseUri, Parser parser) is one of a dozen Jsoup.parse overloads.

tasks.query: look up a tag by its name, returning a new generic tag when the name is not predefined, with optional settings for case sensitivity
tasks.note: Tag.valueOf has three overloads (name; name+settings; name+namespace+settings).

tasks.query: join the string forms of the items of a collection or iterator or array into one string separated by a delimiter
tasks.note: StringUtil.join overloads for Collection, Iterator and String[].

tasks.query: evaluator that tests whether an element's id attribute is equal to a given identifier value
tasks.note: Evaluator.Id.matches; Evaluator has dozens of nested subclasses overriding matches.

tasks.query: builds a path string that uniquely locates a node in the tree, anchored at an id when one is unique, otherwise chaining parent tag and class names plus a sibling position when needed
tasks.note: Element.cssSelector walks up the parents and uses uniqueIdSelector / cssSelectorComponent.

tasks.query: during a traversal of untrusted markup, copy each node into a fresh tree only when its tag passes the allow list, descend into kept containers, and count what is dropped
tasks.note: Cleaner.CleaningVisitor.head implements NodeVisitor.head and copies safe elements, text and data nodes.

tasks.query: lexer step that decides, after an opening angle bracket in markup, whether a start tag, end tag, comment or declaration begins
tasks.note: TokeniserState.TagOpen (an enum constant with a read override) in TokeniserState.java; the symbol listed is the enum itself, which exists under every naming scheme.

tasks.query: turn named and numeric character references in text back into the characters they stand for, optionally treating a missing trailing semicolon as an error
from a CSS query string to matched nodes: the query is tokenised into a chain of evaluators, which are then applied across the tree
cleaning untrusted markup against an allow list: the public entry point, the document-level walk that copies safe nodes, and the rules deciding whether a tag is permitted
after an HTTP response arrives, decode the body bytes to text using the declared or sniffed charset and build the document from them
turning an ampersand sequence in markup text into code points: the tokeniser entry point and the lookup of names in the entity table
